previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of neurogenic bladder from a prior gunshot wound, chronic indwelling Foley catheter, type II diabetes, and right below-knee amputation was admitted for evaluation of two weeks of left-sided flank pain. She was afebrile with no signs of systemic infection. Initial urinalysis showed bacteria, but given her history of chronic urinary colonization with multidrug-resistant organisms and absence of infection markers, antibiotics were discontinued. Imaging of the pelvis and left hip showed no fracture, with findings consistent with degenerative changes and a stable bone island; bursitis was suspected as a pain source. Her anemia was chronic and stable. Pain management was optimized with increased ibuprofen, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up with primary care for ongoing hip pain management and catheter care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ y/o woman with hx gun shot wound c/b 
neurogenic bladder 
s/p urostomy, hx recurrent UTIs, and polysubstance abuse who p/w 
hematuria, pain around her urostomy site, and flank pain x1 day 
at home. Work-up was negative for underlying infection or stone.

===============
ACTIVE ISSUES
===============
# Hematuria/urostomy site pain: Pt presented with new hematuria 
and pain around urostomy site. Initially concerned for UTI given 
positive UA, and she was started on empiric tx with linezolid 
and ciprofloxacin. Linezolid was chosen because last urine cx 
was growing enterococcus and pt has h/o throat swelling with 
penicillin. Given no fevers or leukocytosis and overall well 
appearance on exam, UA was felt to be more consistent with 
colonization and abx were discontinued. Urine culture showed 
fecal contamination. Severe tenderness was new, persistent, and 
well-localized to urostomy site, raising concern for underlying 
complication of urostomy site or renal stones. Urology was 
consulted to evaluate urostomy, and per their recommendation pt 
underwent CT of the abdomen/pelvis for further evaluation. CT 
was negative for nephrolithiasis or fluid collection. For pain 
control pt received standing tylenol and po dilaudid prn, which 
was weaned by time of discharge.  Hematuria had resoolved by 
discharge as had pain, and pt was discharged without 
antibiotics. 

# Polysubstance abuse. Pt reports heavy EtOH hx with last drink 
the day prior to admission. Also with recent crack/cocaine use. 
Pt was started on CIWA scale, with all scores <4 and no ativan 
given during her stay. 

# Pressure ulcer: CT scan showed tissue stranding within R 
gluteal soft tissues c/f cellulitis. On exam, pt had 
pre-existing stage 2 decubitus ulcer with no signs of 
inflammation, not consistent with cellulitis. Wound care nursing 
was consulted on admission for pt's pre-existing ulcer.

================

================
# Hx Diabetes: Patient states she has not required insulin or 
oral medications since she lost 100 lbs. Last Hgb A1C of 5.6% in 
___. Glucose 97 on admission and remained in the 100s 
throughout her stay except for some spurious readings.

# Depression/Aggression: Pt. with history significant for 
depression with suicide attempts as well as aggression towards 
others.  Pt. eloped in the past with central line in place. No 
incidents during this hospitalization.

INDICATION:  ___ with subclavian line placement  // evaluate for line
placement

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest radiographs, most recently of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Single frontal view of the chest.

FINDINGS: 

Right subclavian central catheter terminates at the junction of the right
brachiocephalic vein and the SVC.  Heart size and cardiomediastinal contours
are normal. Lung volumes are low. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or
pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION: 

Right subclavian catheter terminates at the junction of the right
brachiocephalic vein and the SVC.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ w/ neurogenic bladder from gunshot wound s/p urostomy with
ileal diversion p/w severe pain at ostomy site and hematuria  // please
evaluate for pyelonephritis vs stones vs constipation as source of abdominal
and flank pain

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
following intravenous administration of. Coronal and sagittal reformations
were performed. Oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  DLP: 1104 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

CHEST: The lung bases are clear with no pleural effusions, nodules, or masses.
The visualized portion of the heart and pericardium are normal. There is no
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:  Assessment of abdominal viscera is limited without intravenous
contrast. Allowing for this limitation, the liver is. Normal in size a
subcentimeter hypodensity at the dome the liver likely represents a cyst. The
gallbladder is surgically absent. The common bile duct is dilated, consistent
postcholecystectomy change. The spleen, pancreas, and adrenal glands are
unremarkable. The kidneys and are normal in size without evidence of stones or
hydronephrosis.

The distal esophagus is normal appearing with no hiatal hernia.  The stomach
is underdistended, but grossly normal. The small bowel is partially opacified
with contrast, and does not show obstructive mass lesions. The large bowel
contains feces, without evidence of obstructive mass lesions or wall
thickening. The appendix is well visualized and normal appearing. There is no
intraperitoneal free air or free fluid.

There is no aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta.

There are no pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph nodes
by CT size criteria.

PELVIS:  The bladder is surgically absent, and ileal diversion is present. The
uterus and adnexa are unremarkable.  The rectum and sigmoid are unremarkable.
There is no pelvic free fluid. There are no pathologically enlarged pelvic
sidewall or inguinal lymph nodes by CT size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES AND SOFT TISSUES: There are no concerning lytic or
sclerotic lesions seen.  Soft tissue stranding is seen in the right gluteal
soft tissues, which may represent cellulitis.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No evidence of nephrolithiasis.

2.  Moderate fecal loading.

3.  Soft tissue stranding seen within the right gluteal soft tissues, which
may represent cellulitis. Recommend correlation with clinical exam.
